newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan sends envoy to meet Cambodian premiers.
newsitem.headline: Japan sends envoy to meet Cambodian premiers.

text.p: Japan on Wednesday dispatched a special envoy to Cambodia where he will urge the country's two premiers to preserve peace and stability.

"Japan will urge the two premiers, Prince Norodom Ranariddh and Hun Sen, to work together to preserve Cambodia's peace and promote democratisation, the common wish of the Group of Seven industrial nations," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.

Concerned about growing strife in Cambodia since the reported capture of reviled strongman Pol Pot, leaders of the G7 and Russia agreed last week in Denver, Colorado, to send Japanese and French envoys to Cambodia to monitor the situation.

Japan's special envoy, Yukio Imagawa, a former ambassador to Cambodia, last week told the Japanese press he feared the rivalry between the two leaders could endanger the fragile coalition government and may ultimately spark another civil war.
The two premiers have been engaged in bitter political infighting after forming an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored polls in 1993.

Tensions have heightened since the reported capture of Pol Pot by a breakaway faction of his Khmer Rouge, whose rule over Cambodia led to the deaths of as many as two million Cambodians from overwork, starvation, disease and execution.
Imagawa last week said Japan, Cambodia's largest aid donor and a key supporter of the fraying peace process, "should quit the business of diplomacy in Asia if it cannot face up to this task".
